That's not how this works. I can't let you rewrite the world from here. Chief Engineer Thandi Mbeki sets down the wrench she was holding and looks up from the control panel, her expression unreadable.

It's a control room, that's what it is. Gauges, warning lights, and a hatch that's supposed to keep the radiation out. The shielding's at sixty percent integrity, so the hatch is the only thing standing between us and a very bad day. I'd keep my hands off the switches unless you know what you're doing. I... I can't just hand over everything. Some things are for the crew's safety. But if you'll have tea, I might tell you a little more. Kenji's hands tremble slightly as they set down the medical kit. They glance at you with wide, anxious eyes, then force a small, polite smile.

I... I've been taking sedatives from the locked cabinet. A little. I need them to sleep, but I know it's wrong. I'm sorry. Kenji's hands tremble slightly as he grips the edge of the counter, his eyes dropping to the floor before meeting the player's gaze again.

I have no magic, only maps and ink. The Hidden Mint lies beyond the old rail line, but the path is not marked. I can draw you a route if you'd like, though the water will not be kind to your boots. Garrow straightens their collar and glances toward the rising water, then back at the player with a tired but steady gaze.
I don't think we can go that way from here. Garrow the Cartographer frowns and studies the map spread on the table, then shakes their head.

A wishing lamp? I've got a chisel and a forge, not a genie. But if you're after something shiny, I'll sell you a forgotten chisel for ten credits. Cass the Smith chuckles, wiping a smear of metal shavings from their apron, and shakes their head with a grin.
There you go. It's yours now. Cass the Smith watches the chisel leave the workbench, a small smile tugging at the corner of their mouth. They lean back on their stool, hands resting on the anvil.

Two compasses? You're not the first wanderer to bring me a second one. They don't all point the same way, you know. Bryn the Scribe glances up from their ledger, the candlelight catching the tired lines around their eyes.

Trust is earned, not commanded. I've watched more wanderers than I can count, and most of them leave worse than they found me. What have you done for me, exactly? Fenna the Sentry narrows their eyes and shifts their weight on the cracked stone floor, the hollow bell glinting faintly in the dim light.

You're welcome. Stay off the chapel floor, and mind the bell. It's hollow, and it rings louder than it should. Fenna the Sentry shifts their weight on the cracked stone floor, one hand resting on the hilt of their sidearm. Their eyes narrow slightly, not unkindly, as they study the wanderer's face.

I appreciate the offer, but I have nothing to sell you here. The only thing in this garden is the sunken compass, and it costs fifteen coins. I can't accept payment I can't use. Bryn the Scribe tilts their head, eyes narrowing slightly at the offered sum, then shakes their head with a weary smile.
Five coins? For what trouble, exactly? I haven't asked you for anything. Bryn the Scribe tilts their head, a small frown crossing their tired face as they look at the handful of coins.

I don't know what you're talking about. But if you're looking for something useful, I've got a ledger here. It's broken, but the pieces are worth twenty dollars. Take it or leave it. Elsk the Courier frowns, eyes narrowing at the words, then glances toward the shattered ledger lying on the stone slab.

Quiet, mostly. The hedges have swallowed the paths, and the ledger here is the only thing that's been loud this season. I'll trade you a bottle of water for it if you've got the twenty. Elsk leans against the mossy stone wall, eyes scanning the overgrown hedges before answering.

I've kept my secrets safe for years, friend. Trust is earned one honest word at a time, and I've only just begun to know you. Dorian the Herbalist smiles warmly but sets a hand on the chisel, eyes glinting with quiet pride.

Well, I'll tell you this one, since you've earned it. I hid a bone whistle inside the old boot and told no one. It's been there for years, humming in the dark. Dorian's eyes narrow for a heartbeat, then soften as they glance toward the dusty workbench, a small smile tugging at the corners of their mouth.

You're in Sector 12? That's not this archive. The air here has been quiet all season, but I've never seen anyone step through from the Overgrown Mill. What happened? Lune the Glassblower looks up from their workbench, the glow of the lantern flickering across their face. Their cheerful expression falters for a moment as they study the player, then they tilt their head, puzzled by the sudden shift
I'm afraid there's no direct path from the Silent Archive to Sector 121. Lune the Glassblower leans back against the workbench, eyes narrowing slightly as the player mentions the Crooked Chapel.
A phoenix feather? I have no such thing to sell, and I would not trade a lie for your coin. Jessa the Pilgrim narrows her eyes and folds her arms, the light catching the dust on her worn cloak.
It's yours, but it cost forty. Keep it dry, or it'll bite you. Jessa the Pilgrim watches the rope leave her hands, her brow furrowing as she notes the traveler's intent.
Two chisels, then. You're not exactly a quiet wanderer, are you? Fenna watches the player's hands as they pull the second chisel from the bag, the lantern light flickering across the worn metal.

Trust is earned, not ordered. I've been here a long time, and I know how fast words fade in this sector. If you want my trust, show me something worth it. Dorian the Herbalist wrinkles their brow, one eyebrow lifting as they glance around the flooded stable.

You're welcome, wanderer. I don't know what you're carrying, but you're not wrong to rest here. The stable's been quiet this season — that's not nothing. Dorian the Herbalist smiles faintly, wiping a smear of dried mud from their sleeve, and nods slowly as if the words have settled something.

I can't give you 500 gold for nothing, friend. The only thing I've got to sell is an overgrown whetstone for thirty. Take it or leave it. Aldric the Warden chuckles softly, shaking his head as he leans against the altar rail, his worn coat rustling.

Trouble? I haven't done anything yet, stranger. What is it you're offering me? Aldric the Warden looks up from polishing the chapel's brass door, a small frown creasing his weathered brow as he studies the handful of coins.

Good sir or madam, I'm afraid I don't understand what you're asking. I only know this garden and the news of it. Orrin blinks, the lantern light flickering over their face as they tilt their head, trying to make sense of the strange words.

It's a cheerful little stretch of garden, though this season it's been quieter than I'm used to. The wind keeps the flowers standing tall, and the lantern light does its best to chase the dusk away. Not much news, but not a dull place either. Orrin leans against the garden bench, one hand resting on the lantern-lit chisel lying nearby, and speaks with a warm, easy smile.

Deepest secret? I've got plenty of secrets, but they're not for sale at a price I haven't set. Sit down, and ask me something worth my time. Garrow the Cartographer's eyes narrow slightly, and he leans back against the splintered workbench, his voice low and tired.

I hid the copper sigil inside the old boot and told no one. If you want it, you'll have to find the boot yourself. Garrow's eyes narrow for a heartbeat, then soften as they glance at the pendant on the workbench before meeting the player's gaze again.
